mcat_description.short: Modular toilets are factory-built, prefabricated sanitation units — typically constructed from FRP, GI steel, UPVC, or PUF-insulated panels — that are transported to site and installed without civil construction work. They are sold as standalone toilet cabins or toilet-cum-bathroom combo units, in single or multi-seater configurations.
mcat_description.long: A modular toilet is a fully factory-manufactured, plug-and-play sanitation structure built from materials such as FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic), GI steel with PUF insulation, UPVC, or sandwich panels, and delivered ready-to-use to the installation site. Units come pre-fitted with WC (Indian or Western style), wash basin, cistern, overhead water tank provision, ventilation, and electrical connections, requiring only external water and power hookup. They are available as single-seater standalone cabins, toilet-cum-bathroom combos, multi-seater toilet blocks (2–10 seats), and trailer-mounted mobile toilet vans for events and disaster relief. The category is driven by Swachh Bharat Mission demand, construction site labour welfare mandates, and municipal public sanitation infrastructure requirements across India.

market_context: In the Indian B2B market, 'modular toilet' and 'portable toilet' are used interchangeably by buyers and sellers, with 'readymade toilet cabin' also widely used in procurement vocabulary. The dominant construction materials are FRP (Fibre Reinforced Plastic), GI steel with PUF insulation, and UPVC — each suited to different durability and budget requirements. FRP is the most widely manufactured material for single-seater portable units due to its light weight, corrosion resistance, and low cost; GI steel with PUF panels is preferred for semi-permanent and institutional installations requiring better insulation and longevity. The Swachh Bharat Mission has been a major demand driver, creating large-scale government procurement for community and school toilet blocks. Key buyer-side distinctions include: Indian-style WC vs Western commode, toilet-only vs toilet-cum-bathroom combo, single-seater vs multi-seater block, and with/without bio-digester (DRDO-based zero-discharge system). Tata Steel's 'Nestin' and 'EzyNest' brands are recognised trade names in the organised segment; Sintex's 'Sugam' toilet is another known branded product. Manufacturers are concentrated in Rajasthan (Jodhpur), Gujarat (Ahmedabad), NCR (Ghaziabad, Faridabad), Maharashtra (Pune), and Telangana (Hyderabad). BIS standards for sanitary appliances (IS 2556 series) apply to the WC and wash basin fittings within the unit; no single BIS standard governs the prefabricated cabin structure itself, though IS-grade steel materials are specified by buyers in government tenders. GEM (Government e-Marketplace) specifications are referenced by government buyers for handicap-accessible units.
